analysis: All three changed files are test-only: DoctorOperatorDiagnosisTests.swift (lines 77, 86-87, 138-139), StatusCommandRunTests.swift (lines 82-84, 100-141) and the new DaemonStateServedCountTests.swift. No production source, authorization, attestation, encryption, key-handling or coordinator wire code changes in the supplied units. The tests assert revised operator-facing wording for `darkbloom status` and `doctor`: served requests are scoped to the daemon session, counts are output tokens only, and requests that ended early (cancellations_partial_complete) "may be unpaid". That wording is more accurate about billing and does not weaken any threat-model control. The new test writes daemon-state.json to a UUID-named temp directory and removes it afterward. It uses ProviderLoop with attestationSigner nil, with a loopback placeholder coordinator URL (ws://127.0.0.1:0) that is never connected. No real keys, secrets or network I/O are involved. Test sandboxes use a temporary provider home and a stub coordinator. The tests exercise the state-file schema key `cancellations_partial_complete`, but the production implementation (the DaemonStateFile/Status/DoctorRunner changes) is not in the supplied batch. Reviewers of the production side should check that the new stats field is non-sensitive, that the state file keeps owner-only permissions, and that the displayed text does not leak identifiers. Nothing here touches T-041 cache storage or the TB-011 authorization surfaces beyond the existing App Attest fixtures. No findings.
